All our implementations are based on the Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) architecture and adapted from the Fairseq Library (Ott et al., 2019). For the $\mathrm{Zh}\rightarrow \mathrm{En}$ experiments, we utilize the transformer big architecture, while the base and small architectures are used for $\mathrm{De}\rightarrow \mathrm{En}$ and $\mathrm{En}\rightarrow \mathrm{Vi}$ experiments respectively. We use the cosine distance to calculate the read/write supervision signals in the main experiments, and investigate the effects of different divergence types in Section 5.4.2.
